examples.en: There are about eight or nine students in the classroom.
I get home around eight or nine o'clock.

examples.ko: 아이들은 여덟아홉 살 정도 돼 보여요.
examples.en: The kids look about eight or nine years old.

examples.ko: 사과를 여덟아홉 개 샀는데 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought eight or nine apples and ate them all.

examples.ko: 여덟아홉 명이 한 테이블에 앉으면 좁아요.
examples.en: It's cramped if eight or nine people sit at one table.
About eight or nine people came to yesterday's meeting.

explain: 정확한 수를 모를 때 '여덟이나 아홉쯤'이라는 느낌으로 두 수를 붙여 한 단어처럼 써요. '두세 명', '네댓 명'처럼 비슷하게 만든 말이 있고, 뒤에 오는 명·개·살·시 같은 단위는 띄어 써요.
explain_en: You attach two numbers to say 'around eight or nine' when you don't know the exact count. Similar words are '두세 명' and '네댓 명'. Counters such as 명, 개, 살 and 시 that follow are written with a space.

en: all the summer; the whole summer

examples.en: It rained all summer, so it was hard.
My grandmother stayed in the countryside all summer.
I learned swimming the whole summer.

examples.ko: 여름내 더워서 잠을 잘 못 잤어요.
examples.en: It was hot all summer, so I couldn't sleep well.
The kids played at the beach all summer.
I finally picked the tomatoes I grew all summer.

explain: '여름 내내'와 같은 뜻이고, 여름이 시작될 때부터 끝날 때까지 쭉 이어졌다는 느낌이에요. 보통 이미 지나간 일을 말할 때 많이 써요. '여름 동안'보다 계속됐다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '여름 내내' and gives the feeling that something continued from the start to the end of summer. It is mostly used for things that already happened. It feels more continuous than '여름 동안' (during summer).

examples.en: There is a women's clothing section on the third floor of the department store.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 여성복만 팔고 남성복은 없어요.
examples.en: This shop sells only women's clothing, not men's.
Women's clothes come in many sizes, so they are easy to choose.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 여성복 디자이너로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling works as a women's clothing designer.
Excuse me, where is the women's clothing section?
Winter women's clothing is on sale now.

explain: 매장 이름이나 상품 분류에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '남성복'과 '아동복'이에요. 평소 대화에서는 그냥 '여자 옷'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: You often see this word as a store section or product category. Its counterparts are '남성복' (men's clothing) and '아동복' (children's clothing). In casual talk people also just say '여자 옷' (women's clothes).

examples.en: If possible, I want to be treated by a woman doctor.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 병원에는 여의사가 두 분 계세요.
examples.en: There are two women doctors at the clinic in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 어머니는 여의사 선생님을 더 편하게 느끼세요.
examples.en: My mother feels more comfortable with a woman doctor.
The woman doctor explained it kindly.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 어린이 병원의 여의사가 되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to become a woman doctor at a children's hospital.
That woman doctor is popular with patients.

explain: 평소에는 성별을 말하지 않고 '의사 선생님'이라고 해요. '여의사'는 진료받을 때 여자 의사를 원한다는 말처럼 성별이 중요할 때 써요. 의사를 직접 부를 때는 '선생님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Usually people don't mention gender and just say '의사 선생님'. '여의사' is used when gender matters, for example when you want to be treated by a woman. When addressing a doctor directly, you say '선생님'.

examples.en: If there is something you don't know, ask your teacher.
I have to ask an unfamiliar adult for directions.
I asked my grandmother how her health was.
I'll ask my parents first and then decide.
Why don't you ask the professor by email?
May I ask just one more thing?

explain: '물어보다'의 높임말이고, 내가 윗사람에게 물을 때 '께 여쭤보다'로 써요. 윗사람이 물을 때는 '물어보시다'라고 해요. '여쭈다'도 같은 뜻이고, 활용은 '여쭤요/여쭤봐요'처럼 해요.
explain_en: It is the honorific form of '물어보다', used when you ask someone older or higher in status, as in '께 여쭤보다'. When that person asks, you say '물어보시다'. '여쭈다' means the same, and it conjugates as '여쭤요/여쭤봐요'.

examples.en: My train seat faces backward, so I get motion sick.
I feel dizzy when I sit facing backward on a train.

examples.ko: 역방향 좌석 말고 순방향 좌석으로 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me a forward-facing seat, not a backward-facing one.
I took the wrong road and went the opposite way.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 역방향 좌석에 앉기 싫어해요.
examples.en: My friend doesn't like sitting in a backward-facing seat.

examples.ko: 이 숫자들을 끝에서부터 역방향으로 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: Read these numbers in reverse, starting from the end.

explain: 반대말은 '순방향'이에요. 기차나 버스에서 가는 방향과 반대로 앉는 좌석을 말할 때 가장 많이 들어요. 길이나 순서가 거꾸로일 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '순방향' (forward direction). You hear it most when talking about train or bus seats that face away from the direction of travel. It can also describe a route or order that goes backward.

examples.en: We did a restaurant role-play in class today.
I pair up with a friend and practice the role-play.
Thanks to role-plays, speaking became much easier.

examples.ko: 선생님은 역할극으로 주문하는 법을 가르쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher taught us how to order through a role-play.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 역할극 발표를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our class is preparing a role-play presentation.
In the role-play, I took the customer part.

explain: 주로 학교나 학원 수업에서 상황을 정해 놓고 말해 보는 활동을 가리켜요. '역할극을 하다'라고 자주 말해요. 무대에서 하는 '연극'과는 달리 연습과 배움이 목적일 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to a classroom activity where students act out a set situation. People often say '역할극을 하다'. Unlike '연극' (a stage play), it is usually for practice and learning.

examples.en: We painted the baby's room walls light yellow.
A light yellow dress suits spring well.
This flower changes from light yellow to white.

examples.ko: 저는 진한 색보다 연노랑이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like light yellow more than dark colors.
I tried wearing light yellow and sky blue together.
The curtains are light yellow, so the room is bright.

explain: '노랑'보다 옅고 부드러운 색이에요. 초록빛이 도는 '연두'와는 달라요. 대화에서는 '연한 노란색'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is paler and softer than '노랑' (yellow). It differs from '연두', which has a green tint. In conversation people also say '연한 노란색' (pale yellow).

examples.en: In spring, cherry blossoms bloom in pale pink.
A young woman in a light pink skirt is passing by.
We decorated my daughter's room with a light pink bedspread.
Your lips are pale pink, so you look healthy.
The sky turned pale pink because of the sunset.

examples.ko: 연분홍과 연보라를 섞으면 예쁠 것 같아요.
examples.en: Mixing light pink and light purple would look pretty.

explain: '분홍'보다 더 옅고 부드러운 색이에요. 벚꽃이나 노을처럼 은은한 색을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '연분홍빛'처럼 '빛'을 붙이면 그런 색의 느낌이나 분위기를 말해요.
explain_en: It is lighter and softer than '분홍' (pink). It fits subtle colors such as cherry blossoms or a sunset. Adding '빛' as in '연분홍빛' describes the glow or feel of that color.

examples.en: I haven't practiced enough, so I'm nervous about the presentation.
I'm increasing my amount of practice a little every day.
Before an exam, the more practice the better.
With piano, your skill depends on how much you practice.
If you reduce the amount of practice, your body is less tired.
I set my daily practice at two hours.

explain: '많다/적다', '늘리다/줄이다'와 함께 써서 연습을 얼마나 했는지 말해요. '공부량', '운동량'처럼 '-량'이 붙은 말이에요. 시간, 횟수, 쪽수 모두 연습량으로 셀 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it with '많다/적다' and '늘리다/줄이다' to say how much you practiced. It works like '공부량' and '운동량'. Hours, repetitions and pages can all count as 연습량.

examples.en: This is for practice, so you can use it freely.
I bought a practice guitar cheaply.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 연습용 문제를 풀어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried some practice problems before the exam.
I need a notebook to use for practice.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 연습용이라서 점수가 안 나와요.
examples.en: This app is for practice, so it doesn't give a score.
I prepared separate paper for practice.

explain: '-용'은 쓰임새를 나타내요. '연습용'은 실제로 쓰는 것이 아니라 연습하는 데 쓰는 물건이나 자료를 말해요. '실전'과 짝지어 말하면 차이가 분명해져요.
explain_en: The suffix '-용' marks what something is used for. '연습용' refers to things made for practice rather than for the real thing. Contrasting it with '실전' (the real situation) makes the difference clear.

examples.en: I put a pencil holder on the desk.
There are ten ballpoint pens in the pencil holder.
I found a pretty cup to use as a pencil holder.
The pencil holder fell over and all the pens spilled out.
There are scissors in the pencil holder too.
I made this pencil holder myself out of paper.

explain: 책상 위에 세워 두고 연필, 볼펜, 가위 같은 것을 꽂아 두는 통이에요. 가방에 넣고 다니는 '필통'과 달라요. 이름은 연필이지만 다른 문구도 함께 꽂아요.
explain_en: It is a container that stands on a desk and holds pencils, pens and scissors. It differs from a '필통' (pencil case), which you carry in a bag. Despite the name, it holds other stationery too.

examples.en: This card has an annual fee of 30,000 won.

examples.ko: 연회비를 내면 영화표를 할인받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pay the annual fee, you can get a discount on movie tickets.
How much is the annual fee for this club?
I'm looking for a card with no annual fee.
You have to pay an annual fee and there are service charges too.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 연회비로 오만 원이 나갔어요.
examples.en: This month 50,000 won went out as an annual fee.

explain: '연'은 한 해라는 뜻이어서 일 년에 한 번 내는 회원 비용을 말해요. 달마다 내는 것은 '월회비'라고 해요. 카드, 헬스장, 모임, 협회 같은 곳에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '연' means a year, so this is the membership fee you pay once a year. A fee paid monthly is '월회비'. It often comes up with cards, gyms, clubs and associations.

examples.en: Thanks to a passionate teacher, class is fun.
That singer sings passionately on stage.
My younger sibling is passionate about everything.

examples.ko: 열정적인 팬들이 공연장 앞에 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: Enthusiastic fans lined up in front of the concert hall.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 일할 때 아주 열정적이세요.
examples.en: Our team leader is very passionate when working.

examples.ko: 열정적인 사람과 같이 일하면 저도 힘이 나요.
examples.en: When I work with a passionate person, I get energized too.

explain: '열정적인 사람', '열정적으로 말하다'처럼 뒤에 '인/으로/이다'를 붙여 써요. '적극적'은 앞에 나서는 태도를 말하고, '열정적'은 마음이 뜨거운 느낌에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It is used with endings like '인', '으로' or '이다', as in '열정적인 사람' and '열정적으로 말하다'. '적극적' describes a proactive attitude, while '열정적' leans toward a burning, passionate feeling.

examples.en: English grammar feels the hardest to me.
I bought an English grammar book.
There are many English grammar questions on the test.
If you study English grammar, writing gets easier.
With English grammar, understanding matters more than memorizing.
In today's English grammar class, I learned tenses.

explain: '영어 문법'을 줄인 말로, 학교나 학원에서 많이 써요. 말하기 연습인 '영어 회화'와 짝처럼 자주 같이 나와요. 한국어 문법은 '한국어 문법'이나 '국어 문법'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '영어 문법' and is common at schools and academies. It often pairs with '영어 회화' (English conversation). Korean grammar is called '한국어 문법' or '국어 문법'.

examples.en: The main gate was closed, so I went in through the side door.

examples.ko: 이 건물 옆문은 밤에 잠겨 있어요.
examples.en: This building's side door is locked at night.
I'll wait in front of the building's side door.
Excuse me, do you know where the side door is?
Please leave the package at the side door of the house.

examples.ko: 옆문을 열어 두면 바람이 잘 통해요.
examples.en: If you leave the side door open, the air flows well.

explain: '정문', '후문', '뒷문'처럼 문의 위치로 구분해서 부르는 말이에요. 건물이나 집의 옆쪽에 있는 작은 출입구를 가리킬 때 써요. 발음은 [염문]이에요.
explain_en: Like '정문' (main gate), '후문' (rear gate) and '뒷문' (back door), it names a door by its position. It points to a smaller entrance on the side of a building or house. It is pronounced [염문].

examples.en: Please briefly tell me how to prevent the flu.

examples.ko: 가장 좋은 예방법은 손을 자주 씻는 거예요.
examples.en: The best way to prevent it is to wash your hands often.
There is no known way to prevent this disease yet.

examples.ko: 화재 예방법에 대해 선생님이 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher explained how to prevent fires.

examples.ko: 간단한 예방법만 지켜도 건강해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even following simple preventive tips can keep you healthy.
Also be sure to learn how to prevent food poisoning.

explain: 병이나 사고가 생기기 전에 막는 방법이에요. 이미 생긴 뒤에 하는 '치료법', '해결법'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 보통 '감기 예방법'처럼 앞에 무엇을 막는지 붙여요.
explain_en: It means ways to stop illness or accidents before they happen. Remember it as a pair with '치료법' and '해결법', which come after the problem occurs. It usually follows the thing being prevented, as in '감기 예방법'.

examples.en: That child has a really pretty face.
A cute little cafe opened in the alley.
My sister put on neat, pretty makeup and went out.
The packaging is pretty, so it is good for gifts.
The doll that used to be so pretty has become worn out.
The house was small but pretty.

explain: '예쁘다'보다 가볍게 '제법 예쁘다'는 느낌으로 써요. 얼굴, 작은 물건, 가게에 잘 어울려요. 윗사람의 외모에는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It feels lighter than '예쁘다', meaning 'quite pretty'. It suits faces, small objects and shops. It's better not to use it about the looks of someone older or higher in status.

examples.en: I ran into an old love on the street.
When I hear this song, I think of an old love.
He still can't forget his old love.
I got a message from an old love after a long time.
I sorted out and threw away photos of my old love.
I ended up living in the same neighborhood as my old love.

explain: '첫사랑'은 처음 한 사랑이고, '옛사랑'은 지나간 사랑을 그리운 마음으로 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서 직접 '전 애인'이라고 하는 것보다 노래나 글에서 감성적으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: '첫사랑' is your first love, while '옛사랑' is a past love remembered with some longing. It is more sentimental than the direct '전 애인' (ex-partner) and appears often in songs and writing.

examples.ko: 할머니가 어릴 때 옛이야기를 많이 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my grandmother told me many old stories.
Interesting old tales are handed down in our village.

examples.ko: 옛이야기 속 호랑이는 무섭기도 하고 웃기기도 해요.
examples.en: The tiger in old tales is scary but also funny.
The class where we read foreign folk tales was fun.

examples.ko: 아이들이 잠들기 전에 옛이야기를 듣고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The kids want to hear an old story before sleeping.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 옛이야기 열 편이 실려 있어요.
examples.en: This book contains ten old stories.

explain: '옛날이야기'와 같은 뜻인데 더 짧아서 글에서도 자주 보여요. 오래전부터 전해 내려오는 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 발음은 [옌니야기]로 'ㄴ' 소리가 덧나요.
explain_en: It means the same as '옛날이야기' but is shorter and common in writing too. It fits stories passed down from long ago. It is pronounced [옌니야기], with an added 'ㄴ' sound.

examples.ko: 선생님이 칠판에 오각형을 그려 보라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us to draw a pentagon on the board.
A pentagon has five sides.
This building is a pentagon when seen from above.

examples.ko: 별 안에 작은 오각형이 숨어 있어요.
examples.en: A small pentagon is hidden inside the star.
I learned the differences among triangles, squares and pentagons.
I bought a pentagon-shaped plate.

explain: '삼각형, 사각형, 육각형'처럼 각의 수를 앞에 붙여 만드는 말이에요. 발음은 [오가켱]이에요. 일상에서는 '오각형 모양'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Like '삼각형', '사각형' and '육각형', it is built by putting the number of angles first. It is pronounced [오가켱]. In daily talk people also say '오각형 모양' (pentagon shape).

examples.en: Turn left at the five-way intersection you see over there.
My house is near the five-way intersection.
The five-way intersection is complicated and hard to drive through.
It takes about ten minutes to walk to the five-way intersection.
The traffic light at that five-way intersection is broken.
If you follow this road, you'll reach a five-way intersection.

explain: '삼거리', '사거리'와 짝인 말로, 길이 다섯 갈래로 만나는 곳이에요. 약속 장소나 길 설명에서 기준으로 자주 써요. 지명 이름에 붙기도 해요.
explain_en: It belongs with '삼거리' (three-way junction) and '사거리' (four-way intersection), meaning a place where five roads meet. It is often used as a landmark in directions or meeting spots. It can also be part of place names.

examples.en: We did long-distance running in PE class today.
In long-distance running, you should start slowly.
I like sprints more than long-distance running.
My long-distance running time is better than last month.
After long-distance running, I drink enough water.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 가을에 오래달리기 대회가 있어요.
examples.en: Our school has a long-distance running event in autumn.

explain: 학교 체육에서 많이 듣는 종목 이름이에요. 짧은 거리를 빨리 뛰는 '단거리 달리기'와 반대로 오래 쉬지 않고 뛰는 거예요. 한 단어라서 붙여 써요.
explain_en: This is an event name you often hear in school PE. It is the opposite of short sprints, meaning running for a long time without stopping. It is written as one word.

examples.en: The last uphill stretch was really hard.

examples.ko: 자전거로 오르막을 올라갈 때는 기어를 바꿔요.
examples.en: When I go uphill by bike, I change gears.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞은 오르막이라서 겨울에 미끄러워요.
examples.en: The road in front of my house is a slope, so it's slippery in winter.
When it snows, walk slowly on uphill roads.
After the uphill comes a downhill.
I was out of breath on the uphill, so I rested for a moment.

explain: 반대말은 '내리막'이에요. '오르막길'이라고 길 이름처럼 붙여 쓰는 경우도 많아요. 사람의 인생이 좋아졌다 나빠졌다 하는 것도 '오르막 내리막'에 비유해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '내리막' (downhill). It's also common to say '오르막길' (uphill road). People also compare the ups and downs of life to '오르막 내리막'.

examples.en: I am right-handed, but my younger sibling is left-handed.
These scissors are for right-handed people, so they're awkward for me.
If a right-hander writes with the left hand, the writing gets crooked.
Everyone in my family is right-handed.
I'm right-handed, so my right shoulder often hurts.
Most tools are made to suit right-handed people.

explain: 반대말은 '왼손잡이'이고, 손이 아니라 그런 사람을 가리켜요. 도구 이름 뒤에 '용'을 붙여 '오른손잡이용'이라고 하면 오른손잡이를 위해 만든 물건이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '왼손잡이'. It refers to the person, not the hand itself. Adding '용' as in '오른손잡이용' means something made for right-handed people.

examples.en: I ordered omelette rice for lunch.
I drew a heart on the omelette rice with ketchup.
This restaurant is famous for its delicious omelette rice.

examples.ko: 오므라이스는 계란을 얇게 부쳐서 싸야 해요.
examples.en: For omelette rice, you need to fry the egg thin and wrap it.
I tried omelette rice with curry on top.
I can't decide between omelette rice and pork cutlet.

explain: 볶음밥을 달걀로 감싼 요리라서 달걀이 위에 올라간 일반 볶음밥과 달라요. 식당 메뉴 이름으로 자주 보이고, 케첩이나 소스를 얹어서 먹어요. 철자는 '오무라이스'가 아니라 '오므라이스'예요.
explain_en: It is fried rice wrapped in egg, so it differs from plain fried rice with an egg on top. You often see it on restaurant menus, usually with ketchup or sauce. The spelling is '오므라이스', not '오무라이스'.

examples.ko: 저는 오전반이라서 아침 아홉 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: I'm in the morning class, so I start at nine a.m.
The morning class ends at twelve.

examples.ko: 오전반과 오후반 중에 어느 반이 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you prefer, the morning class or the afternoon class?
I want to move to the morning class. Is there a spot?

examples.ko: 동생은 오전반에 다녀서 점심 전에 와요.
examples.en: My younger sibling goes to the morning class, so he comes home before lunch.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에는 오전반 학생이 더 많아요.
examples.en: This semester, there are more students in the morning class.

explain: 학원, 학교, 어린이집에서 시간대로 나눈 반을 말해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '오후반'이고, '저녁반', '주말반'도 같은 방식으로 말해요.
explain_en: It names a class group by time of day at an academy, school or daycare. Its counterpart is '오후반', and '저녁반' and '주말반' are formed the same way.

examples.en: The afternoon class starts at two.
It's hard to get up in the morning, so I signed up for the afternoon class.
Friends in the afternoon class go home in the evening.
I'm in the afternoon class, so I go to the academy after lunch.
Does the tuition change if I switch to the afternoon class?
The afternoon class teacher is different from the morning class teacher.

explain: 점심 이후 시간에 하는 반이에요. 반대말은 '오전반'이고 '저녁반'과도 나눠서 말해요. 학원 등록할 때 시간대를 고르는 말로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a class held after lunch. The opposite is '오전반', and it's also distinguished from '저녁반'. It is often used when choosing a time slot while registering at an academy.

examples.en: My sister-in-law is two years younger than me.
My mother and my sister-in-law cooked together.
I got hand-me-down kids' clothes from my sister-in-law.
I get along very well with my sister-in-law.
I brought a cake on my sister-in-law's birthday.
I called my sister-in-law to ask how she was.

explain: 여자가 남자 형제의 아내를 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요. 오빠의 아내를 직접 부를 때는 '새언니'라고 부르기도 해요. 남자가 형제의 아내를 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: A woman uses it for her brother's wife. When directly addressing her older brother's wife, she may call her '새언니'. A man doesn't use it for his brother's wife.

examples.en: I stuffed some clothes loosely into the travel bag.
Clothes are scattered on the floor.

examples.ko: 이사하기 전에 안 입는 옷가지를 정리했어요.
examples.en: Before moving, I sorted out the clothes I don't wear.
I grabbed just a few pieces of clothing and left.
Please bring me the clothes to wash.
I dry clothes soaked by rain separately.

explain: '옷' 한 벌이 아니라 이것저것 여러 종류의 옷을 가볍게 묶어 말할 때 써요. '옷가지 몇 벌'처럼 말하고, 옷 하나를 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않아요. 짐을 싸거나 빨래, 정리할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it to loosely group several pieces of clothing, not one garment. You say things like '옷가지 몇 벌', and you don't use it for a single item. It often comes up when packing, doing laundry or tidying.

examples.en: The sleeves were long, so I folded them up.
Coffee got on my white sleeve.
The child wiped tears with a sleeve.
Winter sleeves have fur on the inside.
I rolled up my sleeves and started the dishes.
The ends of this shirt's sleeves are worn.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 그냥 '소매'라고 많이 해요. '소매를 걷다', '소매 끝'처럼 자주 써요. 팔 부분만 따로 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often shorten it to just '소매'. It appears in phrases like '소매를 걷다' (roll up one's sleeves) and '소매 끝' (sleeve end). It names just the arm part of a garment.

examples.en: A button came off, so I fixed it temporarily with a safety pin.
Is there a safety pin in your bag?
The skirt waist was loose, so I put in a safety pin.
I pricked my finger on a safety pin and it hurt.
I found a few safety pins in the drawer.
After using a safety pin, keep it closed.

explain: 옷을 임시로 고정하거나 이름표를 달 때 쓰는 작은 핀이에요. 머리에 꽂는 '머리핀'과는 쓰임이 달라요. 찔리기 쉬우니 '찔리다', '꽂다', '닫다'와 같이 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small pin used to hold clothes temporarily or attach a name tag. It's different from a '머리핀' (hairpin). People often use it with verbs like '찔리다' (get pricked), '꽂다' (pin in) and '닫다' (close).

examples.en: That family lives on a remote island.

examples.ko: 배를 타고 한 시간 가면 외딴섬이 나와요.
examples.en: If you go an hour by boat, you reach a remote island.
There are no shops or hospitals on the remote island.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 외딴섬에 혼자 남았어요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie was left alone on a remote island.

examples.ko: 외딴섬이라서 날씨가 나쁘면 배가 안 떠요.
examples.en: It's a remote island, so boats don't run in bad weather.

examples.ko: 외딴섬으로 여행을 가 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever traveled to a remote island?

explain: '외딴'은 다른 곳과 떨어져 있다는 뜻이고 '외딴집', '외딴곳'에도 써요. 사람이 거의 없고 오가기 힘든 섬을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 영화나 소설의 배경으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '외딴' means set apart from other places and also appears in '외딴집' and '외딴곳'. It suits an island with few people and hard to reach. It often appears as a setting in movies and novels.

examples.en: My grandmother adores her granddaughter.
The granddaughter came to visit her maternal grandparents' house during vacation.
I am my grandmother's only granddaughter through her daughter.
The whole family gathered for the granddaughter's first birthday party.
I gave my granddaughter a little allowance.
My granddaughter has already become an elementary school student.

explain: 딸이 낳은 딸을 말해요. 아들이 낳은 딸은 '손녀'나 '친손녀'라고 하고, 딸이 낳은 아들은 '외손자'예요. 일상에서는 그냥 '손녀'라고 할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It means a daughter's daughter. A son's daughter is '손녀' or '친손녀', and a daughter's son is '외손자'. In everyday talk people often just say '손녀'.

examples.ko: 이 집은 외풍이 심해서 겨울에 추워요.
examples.en: This house is very drafty, so it's cold in winter.
I stuck plastic on the window to block the draft.
Because of the draft, my nose gets cold at night.
It's an old house, so drafts come in.
There are drafts and the heating bill is high too.
Drafts come in through gaps in doors or windows.

explain: 집 안으로 들어오는 찬 바람을 말하고, 주로 문틈이나 창틈에서 들어와요. '외풍이 심하다', '외풍을 막다'처럼 자주 써요. 겨울에 오래된 집 이야기를 할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It means cold air coming into a house, mostly through gaps in doors or windows. People often say '외풍이 심하다' (very drafty) and '외풍을 막다' (block drafts). It comes up a lot when talking about old houses in winter.

en: price list; rates table; fare table

examples.en: A parking rate chart is posted at the entrance.

examples.ko: 요금표를 보고 가장 싼 것을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I looked at the price list and chose the cheapest one.
Where is the hair salon's price list posted?
The rates changed, so the price went up.

examples.ko: 요금표에 세금이 포함되어 있는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check whether tax is included in the price list.

examples.ko: 이 요금표는 한 달 전 거예요.
examples.en: This price list is from a month ago.

explain: 주차, 택시, 전화, 미용실처럼 서비스 이용료가 적힌 표를 말해요. 물건 값을 적은 표는 보통 '가격표'라고 해요. 가게나 시설 입구에 붙어 있는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a chart listing fees for services such as parking, taxis, phones or hair salons. A chart for goods is usually called '가격표'. It's often posted at the entrance of a shop or facility.

examples.ko: 동생은 장난감을 혼자 다 가지려는 욕심꾸러기예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a greedy one who wants all the toys.
Like a greedy kid, I ate all the snacks by myself.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 욕심꾸러기라서 나눠 주지 않아요.
examples.en: My son is greedy, so he doesn't share.
I read a fairy tale with a greedy king.
Shall we talk about who the greedy one is?
Don't tease your friend by calling him greedy.

explain: '잠꾸러기', '장난꾸러기'처럼 '-꾸러기'가 붙은 말로, 귀엽게 놀리는 말투로 아이에게 많이 써요. 어른에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요. '욕심쟁이'와 거의 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: Like '잠꾸러기' (sleepyhead) and '장난꾸러기' (prankster), '-꾸러기' makes a teasing but cute label, often used for children. Saying it directly to an adult can be rude. It's used almost the same as '욕심쟁이'.

en: feel a strong desire for; be tempted by

examples.en: I really want that bag these days.
I wanted that position at the company, so I applied.
When I saw my friend's shoes, I wanted them.
If there's something you want, tell me.
With a cake right in front of me, I feel tempted.
I'd like that job, but I'm busy now.

explain: 갖고 싶은 마음이 저절로 생길 때 써요. 그래서 '가방이 욕심나요'처럼 갖고 싶은 것에 '이/가'를 붙여요. 스스로 마음먹고 더 가지려는 '욕심내다'와 달라요. '탐나다'와 비슷하지만 '욕심나다'가 더 일상적이에요.
explain_en: Use it when the wish to have something arises on its own, so the thing you want takes '이/가', as in '가방이 욕심나요'. It differs from '욕심내다', where you deliberately reach for more. It is close to '탐나다' but '욕심나다' feels more everyday.

examples.en: Don't be too greedy from the start.
My younger sibling covets my toys.
If you aim too hard for first place, you actually get nervous.
He has never been greedy about money.

examples.ko: 욕심내서 많이 샀더니 다 못 썼어요.
examples.en: I bought too much out of greed and couldn't use it all.
I got greedy and tried to do it all at once.

explain: 스스로 마음먹고 더 갖거나 이루려고 할 때 써요. '너무 욕심내지 마세요'처럼 충고하는 말에서 특히 많이 들려요. 저절로 갖고 싶어지는 '욕심나다'와 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you deliberately try to get or achieve more. It is especially common in advice like '너무 욕심내지 마세요' (don't be too greedy). Keep it separate from '욕심나다', where the wish arises on its own.

examples.en: Don't act greedy; let's share and eat.

examples.ko: 동화 속 욕심쟁이 할아버지가 벌을 받았어요.
examples.en: The greedy old man in the fairy tale was punished.
My younger sibling is greedy, so he hides snacks.
It feels bad to be called greedy.
Who might be the greedy one in our class?
That person is greedy but kind at heart.

explain: '겁쟁이', '멋쟁이'처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙으면 그런 성격이나 습관이 있는 사람을 말해요. 가볍게 놀리는 말투라서 아이나 가까운 사이에서 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: Like '겁쟁이' (coward) and '멋쟁이' (stylish person), '-쟁이' labels a person with that trait or habit. It has a light, teasing tone, used with children or close friends. Using it for an adult can be rude.
